sections.html:
Columbia County property tax is run by the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division at 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor, Evans, GA 30809. Call 706-261-8299. Hours are 8 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday, except holidays.

That same division takes homestead applications, operates the delinquent tax unit, and posts the county digest and a tax worksheet. Valuation belongs to a separate assessment office. A question about why your house carries the value on the notice does not belong at the commissioner's counter, although staff can send you to the right contact.

  • Bills, payments and payoffs: Tax Commissioner, Property Tax Division.
  • Homestead applications: same office in Evans.
  • Delinquent accounts and sheriff's tax sales: Delinquent Tax Division.
  • Mobile home permits: Planning and Zoning in Evans, or city hall in Grovetown or Harlem.

Columbia is a fast-growing suburban county on the Savannah River, part of the Augusta metro area. Grovetown and Harlem are its cities, and Appling, Evans and Martinez are unincorporated communities. Appling is the legal county seat, but county government actually operates in Evans.

The 2020 census counted 156,010 residents, and the July 2025 estimate of 169,189 is 8.4% higher. There are 65,264 housing units, and owners hold 78.1% of them. A typical owned home is valued at $305,300 and rent averages $1,409. Those figures describe the county as a whole, not any one street.

sections.h2: How a Columbia County tax bill is built
sections.html:
The county's tax worksheet lays out the steps. Multiply fair market value by 40% to get assessed value, then multiply that by the millage rate to get the tax. Millage is stated in dollars for each thousand of assessed value. It comes from the proposed budget divided by the tax digest, which is the total of all assessments.

Exemptions come off before the rate is applied. The county posts a downloadable tax calculation workbook meant for estimating only, and a change in rates, values or fees changes the final amount. Use it to compare scenarios, then get the official figure from the division.

Online payment goes through the county's pay-tax page, where a card adds a third-party processing fee and an eCheck adds $1.50 per item. With an escrow account, check with your lender before paying so the bill is not paid twice.

The county offers a regular exemption plus several for age, disability and military service, and each one reduces the assessed value rather than the market value. The Evans office accepts applications all year. To have the exemption count for the current year, file by April 1.

  • Regular homestead (S1): up to $10,000 off assessed value, for state, county and school purposes, excluding bond taxes and city taxes.
  • Age 62 (L3): $40,000 off for county and school, with net income of both spouses not over $15,000.
  • Local school exemption, age 70 (L6): the school tax on the home and up to three adjoining acres, no income limit.
  • Disabled veteran (S5): $126,526 off, with a VA letter showing 100% service-connected, total and permanent disability, refreshed every three years.
  • Total and permanent disability (L5): $40,000 off, with two physician affidavits and the same $15,000 income cap.
  • Surviving spouse of a military member (SS): $126,526 off, and a full exemption for the spouse of a firefighter or peace officer killed in the line of duty.

For the application, bring a Georgia driver's license with your current address, the vehicle registration card for Columbia County, a recorded deed, and income returns if the exemption tests income. Any change to the deed, a refinance for example, requires a new application.

sections.h2: The January 1 rule when you sell
sections.html:
Under Georgia law, the person who held title on January 1 owes that year's tax. The county tax office does not split the bill between buyer and seller, because that split is a closing matter. A lien stays in the January 1 owner's name unless proof within 90 days of the due date shows the buyer contractually took the tax.

Two practical steps follow. First, read the proration line on the settlement statement and confirm the title company will pay the county rather than leave it for the buyer to find. Second, if a Columbia County bill is still unpaid at closing, ask the Property Tax Division for the exact payoff for the closing date. The division mails each bill to the owner named in its records, so a seller who has moved should confirm the address on file.

The pay-tax page lets you view the tax on a parcel online, which helps you spot a balance before a buyer's title search does. After closing, tell the Property Tax Division about the sale so your homestead exemption is removed, and expect the buyer to file a fresh application of their own with a recorded deed. A pending sale does not change the bill, so keep paying until the closing office has the payoff in hand.

The county starts with a letter or phone call, and if that fails it moves to a levy and a sheriff's tax sale. Most matters are settled without a sale, and the county has one of the highest collection rates in Georgia.

Sheriff's tax sales are public auctions that open at the amount of tax owed, held on the first Tuesday of the month when the office schedules one. The sale notice runs in the Augusta Chronicle legal ads about a month ahead, as well as on the county site.

An owner who is behind should talk to the division before the levy stage. Selling before a sale date is possible, because the payoff is settled from the proceeds at the closing table, but get the numbers in writing first. A cash buyer can close quickly enough to beat a scheduled sale, as long as the title is clear and the payoff is confirmed.

Read the due date on your bill, or ask the division. Georgia's usual window to contest a value is 45 days from the date of the assessment notice, and the notice itself states the deadline for your parcel.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for a Columbia County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: At the Tax Commissioner's Property Tax Division in Evans, 630 Ronald Reagan Drive, Building C, Second Floor. Applications are accepted year-round, but the benefit for the current year requires filing by April 1.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply after refinancing?
faqs.a: Yes. Any change to a deed, a refinance for example, requires a new homestead application.

faqs.q: Is there a Columbia County exemption with no income limit?
faqs.a: Yes. The local school exemption for homeowners 70 or older covers the school tax on the house and up to three contiguous acres, with no income limit.

faqs.q: How often are Columbia County tax sales held?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of the month, when the office schedules one. They are sheriff's tax sales run as auctions, and the notice is published in the Augusta Chronicle about a month earlier.

faqs.q: Can I pay Columbia County property tax online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the county's pay-tax page. A credit card carries a third-party fee, an eCheck carries $1.50 per item, and escrow customers should check with their lender first.
